evidence.sample: VA clinician update: 256 veterans (130 telehealth, 126 in person). Current article abstract: 279 eligible veterans (140 telehealth, 139 in person).
evidence.relationshipNote: The published summaries use different denominators. The approved finding follows the VA update; an identical analytic denominator has not been established.

papers.limitation: The 70 trials cover several therapies, not EMDR alone. Longer-term EMDR data remain limited; included ages extend to 19.

evidence.relationshipNote: Subthreshold medically related PTSD differs from diagnosed PTSD after other trauma. Keep this neutral primary result alongside positive trials.

papers.summary: Among 74 previously hospitalized children aged 4–15 with subthreshold PTSD, EMDR did not outperform care as usual on the primary PTSD outcome through eight months. Parent-reported blood-injection-injury phobia improved more with EMDR.
papers.limitation: Subthreshold medically related PTSD differs from diagnosed PTSD after other trauma. Keep this neutral primary result alongside positive trials.

papers.title: Peer-delivered combined EMD and imagery rescripting for traumatized Chinese university students: a RCT.
papers.authors: Fan H, Zhang J, Wang Y, Yang K, Wang Y, Yang X.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: The study describes an open-label randomized design. Participants reported their own outcomes; hypothesis masking and blinded analysis do not establish masked outcome collection.

evidence.relationshipNote: Trained peers received clinical supervision. The trial tested a combined intervention, with no significant group-by-time effects for depression, anxiety or self-efficacy.

papers.summary: Ninety-five university students were randomized to peer-delivered EMD plus imagery rescripting, imagery rescripting alone or care as usual. Four supervised sessions produced similar changes in depression and anxiety across groups; the combined intervention better maintained resilience gains at follow-up.
papers.limitation: Trained peers received clinical supervision. The trial tested a combined intervention, with no significant group-by-time effects for depression, anxiety or self-efficacy.

papers.limitation: A small, early trial with a mixed adolescent/young-adult sample. Immediate outcomes do not establish durable effects or an exclusively 18–24 result.

papers.limitation: The trauma script rarely produced a cortisol stress response. The predictive contribution was limited and insufficient for clinical application; this is not a gene-expression measurement.

papers.authors: Leen NA, de Weijer AD, van Rooij SJH, Kennis M, Baas JMP, Geuze E.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Molecular or biomarker analysis with combined trauma-focused treatment exposure. No independently verified single- or double-blind randomized molecular comparison is assigned.

evidence.relationshipNote: Treatments included CBT with exposure or EMDR. Exploratory correlations require replication; endocannabinoid concentrations are distinct from gene expression.

papers.summary: Plasma anandamide and 2-AG were measured in 54 veterans with PTSD and 26 combat controls. Pretreatment levels did not predict symptom reduction following trauma-focused therapy; cortisol decreased over time.
papers.limitation: Treatments included CBT with exposure or EMDR. Exploratory correlations require replication; endocannabinoid concentrations are distinct from gene expression.

papers.title: Stress and stress reactivity in posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) following eye movement desensitization (EMD): A randomized controlled trial.
papers.journal: Journal of behavior therapy and experimental psychiatry
papers.authors: Susanty E, Sijbrandij M, van der Mee DJ, Srisayekti W, Suparman Y, Huizink AC.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Publication identity and reported study design checked. Outcome blinding is not established in the material reviewed; no single- or double-blind RCT classification is assigned.

evidence.relationshipNote: Saliva timing depended on participant adherence. This is the same registered component trial as the 2024 neurocognitive report, not an independent replication.

papers.summary: Ninety-one adults with PTSD received eye-movement desensitization or memory retrieval alone. Both groups showed reduced stress reactivity; the study found no specific overall benefit of eye movements and inconsistent cortisol differences.
papers.limitation: Saliva timing depended on participant adherence. This is the same registered component trial as the 2024 neurocognitive report, not an independent replication.
